summary: Anvil receipts are the engine's tamper-evident audit trail: `anvil_receipt` publishes a signed-in-spirit verdict over a run (artifact digest, gate closure digest, checks passed/total, coverage, iterations, cost) and `anvil_receipt_invalidated` retracts a previously published receipt with a reason (`artifact_mutated` | `gate_revoked` | `superseded`). Both are `criticality: safety` and correlate on `session_id_and_sequence` (manifest.json). Darhai currently lists both names in `ACKNOWLEDGED_UNHANDLED_EVENTS` in `src/process/agent/wcore/protocol.ts`, i.e. they are decoded, recognised, and thrown away in silence. The work is to add the two union members, write a pure receipt-ledger reducer that enforces the seven verification rules the 11 adversarial fixtures encode (sequence continuity, idempotent duplicate vs conflicting duplicate, stale replay after invalidation, unknown-critical extension rejection, subcontract version match, invalidation linkage, nested-receipt inertness), register it through the already-wired capability dispatcher at `src/process/agent/wcore/capabilities/index.ts`, and surface only the failure verdicts to the user.
userValue: Real but conditional. When it fires, an Anvil receipt is the difference between "the agent said it finished" and "a gate closed over these exact bytes: 14/14 checks, line coverage 87.5%, artifact sha256:aaa…, scope git:tracked+untracked-excluding-ignored@." — and `anvil_receipt_invalidated` is the engine telling the user that a verdict it already gave is no longer true because the artifact was mutated or the gate was revoked. The concrete user-visible gain in this scope is the failure path: a tampered, conflicting, replayed, or version-mismatched receipt today vanishes without a trace (`ACKNOWLEDGED_UNHANDLED_EVENTS` suppresses even the console warning), and after this work it becomes a visible notice instead of silence. The conditional part is honest: the contract never says under what conditions the engine emits an Anvil receipt to a Desktop host, and `capabilities.anvil_receipts` is `publication_bound`, not `available` — see risks.

In the SAME edit, delete the two lines `'anvil_receipt',` and `'anvil_receipt_invalidated',` plus their `// ── Anvil receipts (tamper-evident audit log) ──` banner from `ACKNOWLEDGED_UNHANDLED_EVENTS` (set shrinks 23 → 21).

handlerWork.change: NEW pure module, no I/O, no Electron, no engine handle. Exports `createAnvilLedger()` returning `{ admit(event: Record<string, unknown>): AnvilVerdict }` plus the types `AnvilVerdict = { outcome: 'accepted' | 'accepted_duplicate' | 'invalidated' | 'rejected'; code: AnvilRejectCode | null; receiptId: string; sequence: number; detail?: string }` and `AnvilRejectCode = 'malformed' | 'version_mismatch' | 'unknown_critical_extension' | 'sequence_gap' | 'sequence_conflict' | 'stale_replay' | 'body_conflict' | 'invalidation_unlinked'`. Rules, in evaluation order, each traceable to a fixture: (1) SHAPE — reject `malformed` unless `origin === 'core/anvil'`, `type` is one of the two, and every field in the schema's `required` array is present with the right primitive type; `terminal_state`, when present on a receipt, must be exactly 'verified'. (2) VERSION — parse `contract_version` as `major.minor`; reject `version_mismatch` when major !== 1 (the host is built against subcontract '1.0', manifest.json → subcontracts.anvil_receipts). (3) UNKNOWN-CRITICAL — reject `unknown_critical_extension` when `required_extensions` is a non-empty array, since this host implements no extensions. (4) SEQUENCE, keyed by `session_id`, shared counter across BOTH event types: expected first sequence is 0; `seq === expectedNext` admits and advances; `seq > expectedNext` rejects `sequence_gap` and marks the session ledger incomplete (do not advance); `seq < lastAdmitted` rejects `stale_replay`; `seq === lastAdmitted` goes to rule 5. (5) REPEAT AT THE SAME SEQUENCE — compute a host canonical hash `hostHash = sha256(JCS(body minus the declared digest field))` and compare against the stored one for that sequence AND compare the declared digest and `event_id`; all three equal → `accepted_duplicate`, no state change; any differ → reject `body_conflict` and quarantine that `receipt_id` (its verdict is no longer trustworthy). (6) INVALIDATION LINKAGE — an `anvil_receipt_invalidated` must name a `receipt_id` already admitted in this session and its `prior_artifact_digest` must equal that receipt's `artifact_digest`; otherwise reject `invalidation_unlinked`. On success mark the receipt invalidated with the reason and return `invalidated`. (7) IRREVERSIBILITY — once a receipt is invalidated or quarantined, no later event may restore it to accepted; a re-admitted identical receipt returns `stale_replay`. (8) BINDING TABLE — keep `declaredDigest -> hostHash`; a declared digest ever seen with a second, different hostHash is `body_conflict`, which is how an altered body is caught on second sighting.
handlerWork.why: This is the whole verification the 11 fixtures define. Keeping it pure and separate from `WCoreAgent` means the fixture tests drive the same function production uses, not a copy. Placing it under `capabilities/` keeps `src/process/agent/wcore/` at its current 11 direct children — AGENTS.md caps a directory at 10 direct children and that directory is already over, so a new sibling file there would make it worse; `capabilities/` goes 2 → 4.

handlerWork.change: NEW module exporting `export const anvilReceiptsCapability: CapabilityHandler` with `name: 'anvil_receipts'` and `handles: ['anvil_receipt', 'anvil_receipt_invalidated']`. It owns one module-level ledger created via `createAnvilLedger()`. `handle(event, ctx)` calls `ledger.admit(event)` and always returns `true` (the capability owns these types; returning false would send them back to the acknowledged-unhandled check and the safety event would go quiet again). On `accepted` / `accepted_duplicate` it calls `ctx.log(...)` only. On `invalidated` and on every `rejected` code it calls `ctx.warn('receipt <id> seq <n>: <code>', event)` AND `ctx.emit({ type: 'anvil_receipt_alert', data: { receiptId, sequence, outcome, code, reason, artifactDigest, detail }, msg_id: '' })`.

testWork.what: Drive every one of the 11 fixtures through `createAnvilLedger().admit()` using the existing helpers `adversarialFixtures('anvil')` and `readFixture()` from `tests/helpers/engineContract.ts`. Assert the exact verdict per fixture: valid-invalidation → [accepted, invalidated]; duplicate-identical → [accepted, accepted_duplicate] with NO state change and no warning; duplicate-conflict → [accepted, rejected/body_conflict] (the two lines differ only in `stamp` verified→conflicting and `receipt_body_digest` 2d5cf64d…→a59a5cc8… — measured); sequence-gap → [rejected/sequence_gap] because the session's first anvil event carries sequence 1; out-of-order → [accepted, invalidated, rejected/sequence_conflict] because line 3 reuses sequence 1 with a different receipt_id/event_id (receipt-desktop-002 / anvil-event-002 — measured); stale-replay → [accepted, invalidated, rejected/stale_replay] and, critically, the receipt must still read invalidated afterwards (line 3 is byte-identical to line 1 — measured — so a naive last-write-wins reducer would silently resurrect a revoked verdict); version-mismatch → [rejected/version_mismatch] on contract_version '2.0' against subcontract '1.0'; unknown-critical-extension → [rejected/unknown_critical_extension] on required_extensions ['future-authority-v2']; altered-body → [rejected/malformed] (terminal_state 'tampered' violates the schema's const 'verified'; verified by running ajv over the bundle — this fixture is the ONLY anvil fixture the published schema rejects on its own); altered-invalidation-body → drive valid-invalidation.jsonl FIRST into the same ledger, then this fixture's line 2, and assert rejected/body_conflict via the declaredDigest→hostHash binding table (the two invalidations differ only in `reason` artifact_mutated→gate_revoked while carrying the identical invalidation_body_digest bc267949… — measured; standalone it passes the schema, so the binding table is the only mechanism that catches it); nested-receipt-inert → feed the whole `sub_agent_event` and assert the ledger is untouched and admit() is never reached for the `inner` receipt. Add a counter-check block that proves the gate is live rather than vacuous: mutate a copy of the good receipt in-memory (bump `sequence` to 5, blank `origin`, set contract_version '2.0') and assert each mutation is rejected with its specific code; and assert `validateEvent(alteredBodyPayload).valid === false` while `validateEvent(goodReceipt).valid === true`, so a future schema swap that stops rejecting cannot pass unnoticed.

Registration and routing, not reducer logic. Assert `surfaceOf('anvil_receipts')` from the contract helper returns exactly the two event types and zero commands, and that `anvilReceiptsCapability.handles` equals that set sorted — so a future engine bump that adds a third anvil event fails here instead of being dropped. Assert `claimedEventTypes()` contains both names and that neither appears in `ACKNOWLEDGED_UNHANDLED_EVENTS` (this duplicates the guard in tests/unit/wcore-capabilityDispatch.test.ts on purpose, because the failure message there names no capability). Build a fake `CapabilityContext` recording emit/warn/log and drive the fixtures through `createDispatcher([anvilReceiptsCapability])` — the exported factory, not a stand-in — asserting: an accepted receipt emits nothing and warns not at all; every rejected code and every invalidation emits exactly one `anvil_receipt_alert` frame with `msg_id: ''` and warns once; and `handle()` returns true for both types in every case, so no anvil event can fall back into the silent-drop path. Add the isolation counter-check: a ledger stub that throws must leave the dispatcher returning false and must not propagate, matching the containment rule in capabilities/types.ts.

Pin the legacy shape. `compat/events/anvil_receipt.legacy.json` is only `{type, sequence, stamp, terminal_state}` and — measured with ajv against the bundle's own core-event.schema.json — it FAILS validation, because the current branch requires receipt_id, event_id, origin, contract_version, session_id, run_id, task_id, artifact_digest, gate_closure_digest and receipt_body_digest. Assert the ledger classifies it `rejected/malformed` and never admits it, and assert it emits an alert rather than being dropped. This is the case where a host could most easily be fooled into showing 'verified' for a receipt carrying no digest at all.

risks: MEASURED AND UNRESOLVED: the body-digest recipe is not in the contract, so a host CANNOT recompute `receipt_body_digest` or `invalidation_body_digest`. I brute-forced it: sha256 over RFC-8785-style canonical JSON of the receipt minus the digest field does not match; nor does any of the 1,048,576 subsets formed by dropping further keys while keeping the four the fixtures prove are covered (stamp, sequence, contract_version, terminal_state); nor sorted vs insertion order, compact vs spaced separators, trailing newline, 13 plausible domain-separation prefixes, or key=value line encodings. Only the wayland-core Anvil producer source or the running binary settles this. Consequence for the plan: the ledger uses its OWN canonical hash and a declaredDigest→hostHash binding table, which catches a body alteration on the SECOND sighting of a digest, not the first. Do not describe this as 'verifying the engine's digest' anywhere in the code or UI.

MEASURED: the published schema catches exactly one of the two tamper fixtures. `altered-body.jsonl` is rejected because the schema pins `terminal_state` to the const 'verified' and the fixture says 'tampered'. `altered-invalidation-body.jsonl` is schema-VALID — its only change is `reason` artifact_mutated→gate_revoked, and the enum admits both — so a first-sight altered invalidation is undetectable by any rule the contract states. The test therefore has to seed the ledger with the authentic invalidation first. That is a legitimate test of a tamper-evident ledger, but it is not proof that a real host would catch a first-sight forgery.

UNKNOWN FROM THE CONTRACT: whether the engine ever emits an Anvil event during an ordinary Darhai turn. `capabilities.anvil_receipts` is `publication_bound`, not `available`, in both manifest.json and the `ready` event's `contract.capabilities` block; `DEFERRED.md` says the producer 'binds the serialized verdict body and immediate post-publication artifact state' and that `anvil_desktop_replay_reducer` and `anvil_persistent_mutation_watcher` are deferred. Nothing states which engine command or workflow publishes a receipt. Only running the binary answers it. If it never fires in Darhai's flow, this lands as correct, tested, unreachable code — which is still the right posture for a safety-class event, but should be stated plainly rather than sold as a feature.

publication_bound means the receipt binds artifact state AT PUBLICATION ONLY. A later filesystem mutation produces no `anvil_receipt_invalidated` (DEFERRED.md is explicit: Core checks immediate post-publication mutation, not the receipt lifetime). Any wording shown to a user must not imply ongoing monitoring, or the app will claim a guarantee the engine does not make.

SEQUENCE DOMAIN IS AMBIGUOUS. manifest.json says `correlation: session_id_and_sequence`, but every fixture uses one session_id, one run_id and one task_id, so the corpus cannot distinguish per-session from per-run or per-task numbering. The plan keys on session_id because the manifest says so; a multi-run session would settle it and only the binary can produce one.

The expected first sequence of 0 is INFERRED, not stated. It comes from the valid fixtures starting at 0 and `sequence-gap.jsonl` being the fixture that starts at 1. If the engine ever emits a session whose first anvil sequence is non-zero (e.g. after a resume), the ledger will call it a gap and quarantine a legitimate receipt. Mitigation to consider at implementation time: treat the first observed sequence as the origin ONLY when the session was resumed, and log loudly either way.

NO FIXTURE EXERCISES SUPERSESSION. `supersedes_receipt_id` appears only in schema/core-event.schema.json and producer-complete.schema.json — grep across the whole bundle finds it in no fixture — and `reason: 'superseded'` likewise has no fixture. The plan's rules treat a superseding receipt as an ordinary new receipt at the next sequence. Whether the superseded receipt should be marked, chained, or removed is a guess until the binary emits one.

`required_extensions` is NOT in the schema's `properties` block. It exists in exactly one file in the entire bundle (adversarial/anvil/unknown-critical-extension.jsonl) and validates only because the branch sets additionalProperties: true. The reject-on-unknown-critical rule is therefore anchored on DEFERRED.md prose ('unknown-critical rejection ... live and proved by serialized replay through the reference host observer'), not on a declared field. If the engine later ships a legitimate extension, this host will start rejecting valid receipts until the list of implemented extensions is filled in.

Contract vs gap-matrix: NO disagreement. tests/fixtures/engine-contract/gap-matrix.json lists both events with capability `anvil_receipts`, criticality `safety`, correlation `session_id_and_sequence`, `implemented: false` — identical to manifest.json. Nothing to reconcile.

IN-MEMORY LEDGER LOSES ITS BINDINGS ON RESTART. The binding table that makes tamper detection work is exactly the state `anvil_desktop_replay_reducer` would persist, and the contract defers it. So a receipt replayed after an app restart is indistinguishable from a first sighting. Persisting the table is a design decision this contract does not authorise and should not be smuggled in without measuring what the engine actually replays.
